bull_bear.body:

- Highly competitive and fragmented market — The Indian pharmaceutical industry is highly fragmented with over 10,000 manufacturers in the organised and unorganised sectors, and approximately 8,000 SMEs make up about 70% of total pharmaceutical units. - Single manufacturing location — Manufacturing is situated at one site at Palghar, Maharashtra (Unit 1, with Unit 2 being added at the same existing facility), concentrating operational, regulatory and licensing exposure at one location.
- Unit 2 commissioning and licensing execution — Unit 2 has been constructed and an application has been made for the required licenses, but it is under commissioning and production is yet to commence, so the stated incremental annual capacity is not yet operating.
- Planned international expansion introduces new competitive and execution exposure — The Company states that as it commences international business it expects competition from major international generic manufacturers, and flags that failure to manage the risks associated with exporting products internationally may adversely affect business, results of operations, financial condition and future prospects.

outlook.body:
- Revenue concentration in tender-based sales to Government Customers (approximately 90% of revenue from operations across the reported periods), so revenue depends on acceptance of bids submitted in competitive procurement processes
- Lengthening working capital cycle - Net Working Capital Days rose from 52 in Fiscal 2023 to 78 in Fiscal 2024, 115 in Fiscal 2025 and 133 in the six months ended September 30, 2025
- Receivables extension - Debtor Days of 97 (Fiscal 2023), 92 (Fiscal 2024), 97 (Fiscal 2025) and 124 in the six months ended September 30, 2025; Creditor Days compressed from 52 (Fiscal 2023) to 20 (Fiscal 2025) and 26 in the six months ended September 30, 2025

- Therapeutic mix shift - Antiparasitic fell from 13.06% of revenue in Fiscal 2023 to 0.08% in the six months ended September 30, 2025 while Blood Related rose to 22.70% and Keratolytic rose from 2.98% to 6.67% over the same span
- Emerging private-customer channel - private customer revenue rose from 0.21% of revenue in Fiscal 2023 to 9.17% in Fiscal 2025 and 10.07% in the six months ended September 30, 2025
- Low leverage - Debt/Equity of 0.01 (Fiscal 2023), 0.08 (Fiscal 2024), 0.06 (Fiscal 2025) and 0.04 at the six months ended September 30, 2025
- Competition and pricing - the Company competes on product portfolio, quality and regulatory compliance, on-time delivery and manufacturing flexibility, and cost-effective manufacturing; competition may result in a decrease in the price paid for its products and services

business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Integrated formulation manufacturing at a single Palghar site: the Company manufactures multiple dosage forms (tablets, capsules, sachets, bottles, external liquids, creams, aerosols, ointments, combination blister packages and external powders) in-house, and describes a versatile facility able to produce multiple products using a combination of processes, allowing the product mix to be changed in response to changes in market demand. Quality control is in-house: the quality control department has the responsibility and authority to approve or reject raw materials, packaging components, intermediate materials, in-process materials, semi-finished products and finished products. Inputs are bought in rather than backward-integrated; cost of material consumed (raw materials plus packing materials) was 48.15% of total expenses in the six months ended September 30, 2025 and 51.79%, 51.83% and 57.03% of total expenses in Fiscals 2025, 2024 and 2023. The Company states it has no long-term contracts with its third-party suppliers; prices are negotiated for each purchase order and it generally has more than one supplier for each raw material. It also purchases stock-in-trade (trading goods purchases of Rs 110.43 million in the six months ended September 30, 2025 and Rs 194.45 million and Rs 33.43 million in Fiscals 2025 and 2024). Downstream, the Palghar facility is equipped with a warehouse; products are sold on a Cost and Freight (CnF) basis; the Company owns no vehicles for transportation and relies on third-party transportation and logistics providers, with finished goods shipped through freight forwarders appointed by the Company or nominated by customers. Freight charges were 2.43% of total expenses in the six months ended September 30, 2025 and 2.93%, 2.78% and 2.48% in Fiscals 2025, 2024 and 2023. Route to market is direct tender-based supply to Government Customers, handled by a dedicated tendering team of 8 personnel as of September 30, 2025; no distributor or retail channel layer is described.

overview.business_model: The company manufactures generic formulations (medicines whose patents have expired, typically used as substitutes for more expensive branded medicines) at its Palghar, Maharashtra facility and supplies them primarily under procurement contracts won through competitive government tenders. Customers are central government projects under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare via GoI agencies, plus state government agencies and bodies (together, Government Customers), alongside a smaller private-customer stream. Products are supplied either under brand names or under generic names depending on customer requirements, and all products (other than those manufactured for others) carry the company's logo. Government Customers contributed 89.93% of revenue from operations in the six months ended September 30, 2025, 90.83% in Fiscal 2025, 98.14% in Fiscal 2024 and 99.79% in Fiscal 2023. Products were supplied to 27 States and Union Territories during the six months ended September 30, 2025 and to 27 States and Union Territories during Fiscal 2025.

strategy_growth.detail: The Company competes in the domestic generics business on therapeutic product categories and, within each category, on dosage strengths and drug delivery. The Indian pharmaceutical industry is highly fragmented. Competition is on the basis of product portfolio, supply (quality, regulatory compliance and financial stability), service (on-time delivery and manufacturing flexibility) and cost-effective manufacturing, and may result in a decrease in prices paid. Some competitors may have substantially greater financial, marketing, technical or other resources. As the international business commences, competition is expected from major international generic manufacturers.
strategy_growth.evidence: "The Indian pharmaceutical industry is highly fragmented, with over 10,000 manufacturers in both the organised and unorganised sectors. Pharmaceutical manufacturing is primarily concentrated in Maharashtra, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Uttarakhand, and Himachal Pradesh. As per the Confederation of Indian Industries (CII), approximately 8,000 small and medium enterprises (SMEs) make up about 70% of the total pharmaceutical units in India. (Source: CareEdge Report)"
strategy_growth.title: Highly competitive market for generic products in India

strategy_growth.detail: Substantially all revenues are generated by sales of generic products, and future profitability depends to a significant extent on continued portfolio expansion through product development activities. The formulation and adaptation of post-patent products is described as complex, time-consuming and costly, characterised by significant upfront costs including product development, obtaining regulatory approvals, building inventory and sales and marketing. New products may not perform as expected, may be less profitable than historically experienced or estimated, may be loss-making, may consume substantial financial resources or divert management attention.
strategy_growth.evidence: "Our portfolio grew from 661 products as of March 31, 2023 to 871 products as of March 31, 2025 ... As of September 30, 2025, our product portfolio comprised 948 products." Product development team of 10 employees as of September 30, 2025.
strategy_growth.title: Dependence on product development activities and continued generic portfolio expansion

strategy_growth.detail: The Company plans to expand its generic formulations business-to-government business internationally to supply foreign government customers in semi-regulated and unregulated countries, excluding the United States, European Union and Japan, by participating in government tenders and obtaining product approvals and import licenses. Disclosed risks include regulatory ambiguity with minimal documentation requirements and sudden enforcement of local standards, unpredictable tender processes with opaque evaluation criteria, delayed payment from government agencies, risk of counterfeit substitution, compliance burden requiring international certifications, political and policy instability, limited market visibility and demand data, local partner and distribution risks and reputational exposure, in addition to customary international risks such as foreign currency volatility, changes in foreign laws and trade restrictions, tariffs, quotas, anti-dumping or countervailing measures and economic instability or political unrest.
strategy_growth.evidence: "Payment cycles under government schemes in these semi-regulated or unregulated countries can stretch from several months to even a year."; "We, as exporter of products into the semi-regulated or unregulated countries, are required to maintain international certifications such as WHO-GMP and ISO in order to be eligible to participate in government schemes." Capacity is heavily under-used before a second unit is added: Unit 1 utilisation in the six months ended September 30, 2025 was 22.22% on tablets (installed 9,500 million), 1.16% on capsules (1,500 million), 5.72% on sachets, 10.60% on syrups, 6.80% on external liquid, 0.40% on aerosol and 0.60% on external powder, with no production at all on combi blister packs (30 million packets), kits (0.6 million packets) or surgical dressing (5.00 million sachets); tablets ran at 53.24% in Fiscal 2025 and 40.55% in Fiscal 2024.

Attrition 18.40% / 25.00% / 38.33% / 17.20% on average headcount of 282 / 277 / 264 / 268, product development attrition 35.29% then 40.00% in each of three periods on a 10-person team, and no key man insurance; two Executive Directors ceased on July 01 and July 10, 2025; two Chief Financial Officers and two Company Secretaries appear across the restated periods; all Promoters, who are also Directors, state they have no prior listed-entity experience; Krishiv Rajesh Doshi, aged 23 and son of the Chairman and Managing Director, joined the Board on August 11, 2025.

Rajesh Vasantray Doshi holds 49,862,280 of 49,864,030 pre-Offer shares (99.99%) with only 8 shareholders on the register and nil pledge, and has guaranteed the Rs 500.00 million Union Bank of India facility for NIL consideration. Against that, the Offer for Sale of up to 9,100,000 shares is entirely his against a Fresh Issue of up to 5,000,000, substantially the whole equity base was issued to him at par for consideration other than cash on September 18, 2020, post-Offer shareholding and the entire Minimum Promoters' Contribution lock-in table print as placeholders, and no auditor-certified average cost of acquisition figure appears in the routed text.

The DRHP states no market share and says there are no directly comparable peers fully aligned with its product profile and B2G model, naming Ajanta Pharma, Syncom Formulations (India) and Windlas Biotech only for the industry P/E range of 25.70 to 35.25 (average 28.88). It cites the CareEdge Report that the Indian pharmaceutical industry has over 10,000 manufacturers with roughly 8,000 SMEs making up about 70% of units, and flags DPCO and NPPA ceiling-price revisions on over 923 scheduled formulations as leaving minimal pricing flexibility - in a channel where price is the award criterion.

Unit 2 constructed at Rs 358.07 million but licences applied for and not received and production not commenced; the cosmetics line of nine planned products has the FDA Maharashtra licence dated May 27, 2025 valid to May 26, 2030 but production has not started; the international B2G plan targets semi-regulated and unregulated countries where the DRHP itself notes payment cycles can stretch from several months to even a year; and the Saykha API plots bought for Rs 76,250,734 in 2021 remain unbuilt with a GIDC extension to March 31, 2027 applied for and not granted.

red_flags: Three criminal prosecutions under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 arising from drugs declared Not of Standard Quality, in a business whose product is medicine supplied to public health systems. Complaint no. STC/0000213/2024 dated March 01, 2024 was filed by the Drug Inspector, Dindigul Zone, Madurai before the Judicial Magistrate No. 1, Dindigul under Section 32(1) alleging contravention of Section 18(a)(i) in respect of meclobic capsules batch no. CAX23001AL manufactured in January 2023, and was stayed by the Madras High Court, Madurai Bench by interim orders dated January 06, 2025 and January 23, 2025; complaint no. 219585/2019 dated September 19, 2019 by the Drug Inspector, West Zone, Mumbai concerns paracetamol tablets IP 500 mg batch no. APC6036AL manufactured in September 2016; and R. Criminal Case No. 404029/2008 dated September 24, 2008 was filed by the Drug Inspector, Pune. The DRHP records six further criminal proceedings plus one material civil litigation against Promoter, Chairman and Managing Director Rajesh Vasantray Doshi (seven proceedings against Promoters, aggregating Rs 20.00 million), nil against Directors, Key Managerial Personnel and Senior Management, and states no provision has been made for any pending legal proceeding.

The Company operated without the statutorily required board for over three years and the matter was still unresolved days before this DRHP. Paid-up capital crossed Rs 100 million with effect from September 18, 2020, triggering Section 149(4) of the Companies Act, 2013 read with Rule 4 of the Companies (Appointment and Qualifications of Directors) Rules, 2014; the Independent Directors were appointed only on December 13, 2023, and in the interim the Company was also unable to constitute the audit committee and the nomination and remuneration committee. An adjudication and compounding application in Form GNL-1 bearing SRN No. AC0216592 was filed on December 21, 2025, and as on the date of this January 3, 2026 DRHP no notice, order or communication had been received from the Registrar. The same disclosure records that Form CRA-2 and Form CRA-4 for the cost auditor appointment and the cost audit report were not filed within prescribed timelines for financial years 2022, 2023 and 2024, and that transfer of unspent CSR was delayed beyond the stipulated 30 days for financial year 2022-23.

Profit is not becoming cash, and the sole quantified use of the Fresh Issue is to fund that gap. CFO fell Rs 332.85 million to Rs 198.91 million to Rs 107.67 million across Fiscals 2023 to 2025 while PAT rose Rs 222.50 million to Rs 412.66 million; trade receivables reached Rs 857.18 million at September 30, 2025, equal to 76.10% of the six-month revenue from operations, with debtor days at 124; and the DRHP proposes Rs 725.00 million of Net Proceeds for incremental working capital in Fiscal 2027 on funding requirements that are stated to be based on management estimates in view of past expenditures and to have not been appraised by any bank or financial institution. Entire deployment is scheduled in Fiscal 2027, with Nil in Fiscal 2026, the general corporate purposes amount is unquantified within a 25% of Gross Proceeds cap, and no asset is created by the Fresh Issue.

The register is effectively one person and the exit is entirely his. Rajesh Vasantray Doshi holds 49,862,280 of the 49,864,030 pre-Offer Equity Shares (99.99%), the Company has 8 shareholders in total with the public category holding 750 shares, and the Offer for Sale of up to 9,100,000 Equity Shares is entirely by him against a Fresh Issue of up to 5,000,000. Substantially the whole equity base - 49,853,780 shares allotted on September 18, 2020 at par of Rs 10 for consideration other than cash - was issued to him against the takeover of the Hindustan Laboratories sole proprietorship for Rs 498,537,800 under a Business Takeover Agreement dated May 01, 2020, and the securities premium account before the Offer is Nil. The DRHP's own risk factor states Promoters currently own 100% of outstanding Equity Shares and will continue to hold a substantial post-Offer stake, with the post-Offer percentage left blank.

The promoter is simultaneously landlord, licensor, lender and security-deposit counterparty of the company he owns 99.99% of. Beyond the Unit 1 and Unit 2 leases and the trademark royalty, the restated related-party note shows rent paid to Rajesh V Doshi of Rs 103.7 lakhs in each of Fiscals 2023, 2024 and 2025 and Rs 79.8 lakhs in H1 Fiscal 2026, rent to Bhavna R Doshi of Rs 110.5 lakhs a year, rent to Rajesh V Doshi HUF of Rs 10.7 lakhs a year, a security deposit of Rs 450.0 lakhs paid in Fiscal 2025 that took the security deposit receivable from him from Rs 224.9 lakhs to Rs 674.9 lakhs, loans accepted of Rs 1,710.0 lakhs (Fiscal 2024) and Rs 2,490.7 lakhs (Fiscal 2025) against loans paid of Rs 1,256.8 lakhs and Rs 2,280.4 lakhs, and a loan payable of Rs 385.0 lakhs outstanding at September 30, 2025 that is interest-free and repayable on demand. He has also guaranteed the Rs 500.00 million Union Bank of India facility for NIL consideration, repayable on demand.

The statutory auditor was replaced mid-stream because the incumbent lacked a peer review certificate, and the successor's registration number is printed two different ways in the same document. TMG & Associates, appointed at the AGM on September 30, 2022, tendered its resignation on August 25, 2023 because the firm had not obtained its peer review certificate; JAIN V & CO was appointed on September 30, 2023 to fill the casual vacancy and re-appointed at the AGM on September 30, 2024. The DRHP cites JAIN V & CO, Chartered Accountants having FRN No. 116303W in the eligibility certificate reference against Firm Registration No: 116306W in the examination report on the Restated Financial Information. The Fiscal 2024 CARO annexure separately records the predecessor's resignation as an observation.

The Company's credit ratings were suspended for three years for non-submission of data to the rating agencies - disclosed by the issuer as a live risk that any such failure could again result in suspension - in a business where Rs 328.37 million of tender bank guarantees at September 30, 2025 and a Rs 500.00 million sanctioned non-fund-based limit are the mechanism by which contracts are won. The present ratings, CARE BBB+; Stable and CARE A3+, date only from the letter of March 12, 2025.

A capital commitment made in 2021 has been shelved indefinitely with the land still on the books and a penalty exposure open. Plots DP/87 and DP/88 admeasuring 30,008.160 sq. meters at Saykha Industrial Estate, Bharuch were acquired from GIDC under an agreement dated September 24, 2021 with possession on September 30, 2021, on a 99-year lease at a lumpsum of Rs 76,250,734; environmental clearance from SEIAA Gujarat and hazardous waste disposal approval from BEIL Infrastructure Limited were obtained, but construction has not commenced and management has deferred it citing market conditions, connectivity constraints, API-sector uncertainty and the capital outlay required. The plots were not utilised within the GIDC-prescribed timeframe, an extension to March 31, 2027 has been applied for and not granted, and the DRHP warns GIDC may levy non-utilisation penalties and/or evict the Company.

Internal disclosures do not reconcile with each other in three separate places. Headcount: the risk factors state that as on September 30, 2025 the Company had 616 employees working in its manufacturing facilities, while the attrition disclosure for the same period gives an average number of employees of 268 (against 264, 277 and 282 in Fiscals 2025, 2024 and 2023), and total employee strength is not disclosed at all. Directorship dates: Independent Director Dambarudhar Sahu is shown as Director since August 11, 2025 in the Board table but as appointed Additional Independent Director on August 11, 2024 in the changes-to-the-Board table. Royalty: the trademark licence consideration is stated as Rs 125,000 per month under a deed dated April 01, 2025 valid five years to April 01, 2030 in Interest of Directors, but as Rs 100,000 per month for April 2025 to September 2025 rising to Rs 125,000 from October 2025 to March 2030 in Interest of our Promoters.
strengths_observed: Three-year profit build with margin expansion: revenue from operations Rs 1,723.39 million (Fiscal 2023) to Rs 1,863.74 million (Fiscal 2024) to Rs 2,197.46 million (Fiscal 2025); PAT Rs 222.50 million to Rs 341.38 million to Rs 412.66 million; EBITDA margin 17.81% to 23.66% to 24.52% on the KPI-comparison series reproduced from the restated P&L; EPS Rs 4.46 / 6.85 / 8.28.

Effectively debt-free at the balance sheet date: total borrowings were Rs 38.50 million as on September 30, 2025, stated in the DRHP as 100% unsecured and being the interest-free promoter loan, against net worth of Rs 1,970.09 million; the Rs 150.00 million fund-based cash credit sub-limit remained entirely unutilised as at November 30, 2025 and none of the promoter shares are pledged or otherwise encumbered.

Capital efficiency held through the three restated Fiscals without leverage: RoCE 31.76% (Fiscal 2023), 37.25% (Fiscal 2024) and 33.13% (Fiscal 2025); RoNW 24.18%, 28.39% and 26.11%, with net worth compounding from Rs 1,031.52 million to Rs 1,787.39 million over the same period.

The registration base is wide and still widening: the product portfolio grew from 661 products at March 31, 2023 to 749, then 871 at March 31, 2025 and 948 as of September 30, 2025, with 17, 88, 122 and 77 new products introduced across the four periods; the Company holds Food & Drugs Administration (Maharashtra State) registrations to manufacture 948 products and approvals for more than 900 formulations.

Tender win rate improved across the restated periods: 46 of 66 bids won (69.70%) in Fiscal 2023, 59 of 99 (59.60%) in Fiscal 2024, 55 of 86 (63.95%) in Fiscal 2025 and 22 of 28 (78.57%) in the six months ended September 30, 2025, with a further 20 bids awaiting results at that date.

The private-customer channel has gone from immaterial to a real second leg: private customers were Rs 3.58 million / 0.21% of revenue from operations in Fiscal 2023, 1.86% in Fiscal 2024, 9.17% in Fiscal 2025 and Rs 113.39 million / 10.07% in the six months ended September 30, 2025.

Reach across the buyer base is national rather than single-state: products were supplied to 27 States and Union Territories in Fiscal 2025 and to 27 States and Union Territories in the six months ended September 30, 2025, and no single state exceeded 26.16% of revenue in Fiscal 2024 or 23.31% in Fiscal 2025.

Rated and re-rated after an earlier lapse: CareEdge assigned CARE BBB+; Stable on Long Term Bank Facilities and CARE A3+ on Short Term Bank Facilities by rating letter dated March 12, 2025, following the three-year period in which the Company's ratings stood suspended for non-submission of data.

The physical expansion is already paid for rather than proposed: Unit 2 at Palghar (2,842 square meters) has been constructed with project cost of Rs 358.07 million incurred as of September 30, 2025 and Rs 370.43 million sitting in capital work-in-progress, and no part of the Fresh Issue is earmarked for it - capital expenditure of Rs 40.94 million, Rs 49.20 million, Rs 262.24 million and Rs 114.05 million across the four periods was funded without term debt.

Insurance cover was materially raised in the latest period: sum insured of assets rose to Rs 693.47 million against Rs 830.38 million of insurable assets, taking coverage to 83.54% at September 30, 2025 from 46.57% at March 31, 2025, 61.80% at March 31, 2024 and 43.88% at March 31, 2023.

Related-party accounting is fully reconciled in this filing: all 112 related-party lines across H1 Fiscal 2026 and Fiscals 2025, 2024 and 2023 carry stated amounts with none left null, and promoter borrowings were repaid within the same year they were taken (Rs 2,490.7 lakhs accepted against Rs 2,280.4 lakhs repaid in Fiscal 2025; Group Company Hindustan Capital Private Limited Rs 816.8 lakhs accepted and Rs 816.8 lakhs repaid in Fiscal 2025).
